_about: Human-curated evidence register and conflict registry for the KO-3201 demonstration case. Each excerpt is copied from the cited location; nothing here corrects raw data. Curated 2026-10-02 during prototype build (internal review, not a domain-expert review).

evidence.title: Register entry
evidence.excerpt: KO-3201 · ZCU · Class A · occurred 2026-04-29 · Class A Eq. Breakdown · downtime 32 h · actual loss 1,584 k US$ · potential loss 475.2 k US$ · status CA/PA EXECUTION · RCA due 2026-06-13 · PIC (RCA) REL-05

evidence.title: Monitored limits (as currently recorded)
evidence.excerpt: DE Radial Vibration (micron) 45 / 75 · Lube Oil Water Content (ppm) 500 / 1500 · Lube Oil Supply Press (barg) 1.4 / 1.1 · Bearing Metal Temp (°C) 95 / 110. No effective date recorded.

evidence.title: Weekly condition: ALARM from 11 Feb
evidence.excerpt: Health Status ALARM every week from 2026-02-11 to 2026-04-22. Water content 501 ppm (11 Feb) rising to 1,373 ppm (22 Apr); DE vibration 37.7 → 71.7 micron; supply pressure 1.635 → 1.122 barg.

evidence.title: Weekly reading at trip
evidence.excerpt: 2026-04-29: vibration 76.5 micron · water 1,530 ppm · supply pressure 1.078 barg · bearing temp 112.2 °C · TRIP · 'FAILURE — High Radial Vibration Trip (Bearing Distress); unplanned downtime 32.0 h'

evidence.title: Condition after repair
evidence.excerpt: NORMAL on every reading 2026-05-06 to 2026-06-03 (vibration 26.9–27.7 micron, water 242–248 ppm). Last reading in file: 2026-06-03.

evidence.title: Hourly PI series around the trip
evidence.excerpt: KO3201_VIB (PI unit MM/S) stays 28.1–29.4 from 22 to 26 Apr, rises to 44.2 on 27 Apr and 72.67 at 06:00 on 29 Apr. RUN_STATUS OFF from 07:00 29 Apr to 14:00 30 Apr (32 h).

evidence.title: RCA chronology
evidence.excerpt: 27-Apr: DE radial vibration trending up (from 28 to 52 micron over 5 days). 29-Apr 06:40: tripped at high-high 75 micron. 08:10: lube-oil water 1,800 ppm (spec < 500). 18:00: babbitt wiped; lube-oil cooler tube leak confirmed. 30-Apr 14:40: new bearing, oil flushed, tube plugged, restarted.

evidence.title: RCA historical evidence
evidence.excerpt: Vibration baseline 25–30 micron; steady rise over 5 days preceding the trip. Lube-oil water content had drifted above 500 ppm for ~2 weeks without an online alarm.

evidence.title: 4P parameter verification
evidence.excerpt: P1 vibration NG (75 vs 45 alarm) · P2 water NG (1,800 vs < 500 ppm) · P3 supply pressure G ('Header pressure 1.8 barg — within normal band') · P4 bearing life G ('3 years vs 6-year design') · P5 surge margin G.

evidence.loc: RCA deck · slide 7 (4M+1E and root cause)
evidence.title: Root cause as documented
evidence.excerpt: X1 no online water-in-oil monitoring (NG) · X2 cooler integrity not trended (NG) · X3 'Alert at 60 micron gave little lead time before 75 micron trip' (NG). Root cause: babbitt distress from degraded oil film due to water ingress via a leaking lube-oil cooler tube, undetected without online water-in-oil monitoring.

evidence.title: Corrective & pro-active actions
evidence.excerpt: P2 Repair cooler tube — 30-Apr-2026 — STA-02 — Closed · X1 Install online water-in-oil sensor on KO-3201 — 30-Jun-2026 — REL-05 — In Progress · P2 Retube cooler at next TA — 31-Oct-2026 — STA-02 — Open · X1 Online water-in-oil monitoring on KO-3202/3203 — 30-Sep-2026 — REL-05 — Open

evidence.title: Preventive actions (no status recorded)
evidence.excerpt: X3 Tighten KO-3201 vibration alert to 45 micron & shorten trend-review cadence — 30-May-2026 — REL-05 · X2 Add cooler dP & conductivity trend to reliability dashboard — 30-Jun-2026 — REL-02. Risk countermeasure: start-up alarm suppression timer — 30-May-2026. PM-1 weekly water/particle count; PM-2 6-monthly cooler leak test; PM-3 daily vibration trend review.

evidence.title: Performance summary
evidence.excerpt: 26 weekly readings · downtime 32 h · availability 99.27 % (period 4,368 h) · ALARM 11 · TRIP 1 · NORMAL 14 · PM compliance 92 % · production loss 1,760 t · estimated loss 1,584 k USD (production loss × product price).

evidence.title: Design life
evidence.excerpt: Design Life: 5 years (bearing) / 24 months (seal element). The same value appears on all five equipment files.

a.says: Alert was 60 micron before the trip

b.says: Equipment Info lists alarm 45 micron (no effective date)

conflicts.note: Slide 10 plans tightening the alert to 45 micron by 30-May-2026, so Equipment Info may show the post-change limit. Effective date is not recorded; historical ALARM labels cannot be assumed to use 45.

a.says: RCA: rise from 28 to 52 micron over ~5 days before 27 Apr

b.says: Weekly record: 71.7 micron on 22 Apr, ALARM since 11 Feb

conflicts.note: The hourly PI series (EV-06) agrees with the RCA's late rise (≈29 until 26 Apr). Weekly and hourly series may come from different measurement points or definitions; the weekly replay must not be called an operational reconstruction.

conflicts.topic: How long water content exceeded 500 ppm

b.says: Weekly record: above 500 ppm from 11 Feb (~11 weeks)

conflicts.note: Matters for the effectiveness rule of the water-in-oil monitoring action: which sampling record is authoritative?

a.says: RCA 4P: header pressure 1.8 barg, within normal band (G)

b.says: Weekly record: 1.078 barg at trip week, below the 1.1 trip limit

conflicts.note: If the weekly value is valid, P3 'G' would need re-assessment. Possibly different measurement point (header vs bearing supply).
Both sources agree the bearing (3 years in service) was within life. Equipment Info carries an identical design-life string for all five assets, which suggests a template default.

conflicts.topic: Vibration units: weekly micron vs hourly MM/S

a.says: Weekly DE Radial Vibration in micron

b.says: PI tag KO3201_VIB engineering unit MM/S, values 25–73

conflicts.note: Displacement (micron) and velocity (mm/s) are not convertible without frequency content. The PI magnitudes resemble micron values, so the PI unit label itself needs confirmation. Rule applied: never overlay or convert.

conflicts.note: Values kept as recorded (all 85 OFF rows in the five files behave the same). Sensor semantics must be confirmed before any energy conversion.
